plaintext.source: No clear copy of this letter in the file.

transcription.notes: One key-free reader; 17 corrections on enlarged strips, logged. A third hand. Read provisionally: B count 147 of 154, no margin.

system.summary: Simple substitution of Italian: 20 signs for the 20 letters a b c d e f g h i l m n o p q r s t u/v z. No word breaks, nulls, homophones or code groups in any page read. The same table in 1630 and 1636; the letters to Forni use another.

diacritics.note: In cc. 73-74 only, a small caret above a sign doubles the letter. Balls and dots on strokes are pen style.

system.doubled_letters: written twice in 1630; a caret above the sign in 1636
system.notes: Weak shapes: n and h; tailed t and g in one hand; a closed like c and c open like a in places. Those calls rest on sense.

prior_solution.where: Later clear copies at c. 15 and c. 22 of Lettera T cover c. 13-14 and c. 23r; the writer could read this cipher. For the other letters nothing is settled: Doglio's edition (1967), the Reggio Emilia inventory, the 1843 Memorie and Raviola (2014) were not opened (3 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1567) and the rules; AI language-model agents located the letters, transcribed, built the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (strips, shape classifiers, held-out test, counts)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: Thirteen letters located on Lodovico; neighbouring leaves of Lettera T opened and found without cipher.
c. 23r transcribed sign by sign; checked by clusters (338/360) and a k-fold classifier (326/399) with no language.
Key built by aligning c. 23r with c. 22, a later clear copy, and frozen before c. 13r was transcribed.
Held-out c. 13r against c. 15r: 286/289 visual, 232/289 machine with no language, against at best 43.6% for shuffled tables.
cc. 9, 11, 16, 20 retranscribed from a key-free copy against a shuffled sign sheet; 39 corrections on crops; whole-word repairs withdrawn.
Key applied to the 1630 letters and, unchanged, to cc. 73-74 of 1636 from a key-free copy.
c. 53 attacked as a simple substitution on a rough copy; a control on known Italian recovered 429 of 573 letters; c. 53 gave no Italian.
Final independent check: 2340 signs read before the solver text was opened, 36 differences (1.5%), about 4 solver errors after zoom. Not key-free.
Fresh sign-first read of c. 7r and c. 74r rows 8-15 on strips recut to the paper edge, by an agent who knew the key and had seen the text: 5 changes in c. 7r, none in the 233 signs of c. 74r.
Doglio, the Reggio inventory, the 1843 Memorie and Raviola 2014 identified but not opened.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key built by aligning the cipher of c. 23r with c. 22, a later clear copy in the same file; not by cryptanalysis. Tested on held-out c. 13r against c. 15r.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 4860 sign positions in the 7 letters read and the 8 lines of c. 13r. The unread cipher is not counted: c. 53 is about 570 signs, and the rest of cc. 13-14, c. 54, c. 72, c. 4 and cc. 5-6 are not measured, so the share is a rough guess. Per letter, words reading as sense are in NOTES.md and in read_share (count B).

texts.label: c. 7r, 7 Feb 1630

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. The cipher reads as connected Italian sentences: the prince of Correggio is held by the Germans and ordered to Sabbioneta, and the agent is told to act first and then serve Modena. The decryption matches the reading line for line. There is one real hole, the doubtful "compiamo" (translated as "feel for" as a guess), plus three letters restored at a tear or edge.

texts.summary: The prince of Correggio is held prisoner in his own town by the Germans, under order to appear at Sabbioneta within 25 days. The agent is told to move first, and that once the prince's ruin is beyond repair he must serve Modena.

texts.label: cc. 9r-9v, 15 Feb 1630

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. About 250 words of cipher that run as coherent Italian prose, and the English follows it closely, including the Correggio and Castiglione proposal and the warning about Mirandola. There are scattered holes: "roliet" is unresolved and leaves the clause after "Non vi scordate di" unclear, the clear word "Feudo" is doubtful, and about six signs were changed or restored by the editor (aongiunture, oaulato, confidenui, risul[u]zione, n[o]i, nego[z]io).

texts.summary: The duke suspects the court of feeding him hopes in order to use him. Rumour says the Germans have taken the fief of the prince of Castiglione. The agent is to propose Correggio for Modena and Castiglione for the duke of Guastalla, and to watch Mirandola.

texts.label: c. 11r, 15 Feb 1630

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. A short passage that reads as complete, grammatical Italian about the duke of Mirandola's risk and the order to enlarge the danger to His Excellency, and it matches the decryption. The only editorial change is "proaessi" to processi. "Qualco" is kept as the writer wrote it. Who "Sua Eccellenza" refers to is not identified.

texts.summary: The duke of Mirandola is at risk of a trial too. The agent is to warn His Excellency and enlarge the danger.

texts.label: c. 13r, 22 Feb 1630, first 8 cipher lines

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. Only eight cipher lines were read, and they make coherent Italian about the marchese's offer of fifteen thousand foot and four hundred horse. The passage begins and ends mid-sentence because it is an extract. There are two weak spots: two lost signs restored as "fi[n g]iunto" and the doubtful clear word "fermo". The decryption file does not mark where the clear words "Supponiamo che" fall, but the reading places them correctly.

texts.summary: The marchese di Villafranca has offered the Emperor and his ministers the duke's person and states, up to fifteen thousand foot and four hundred horse. Transcription job: c. 15 covers it. Held-out test of the key.
texts.note: Words 58: A 58, B 58, C 55. Read in part because only 8 lines are transcribed. read_share is the share of those lines.

texts.label: cc. 16r-16v, 22 Feb 1630

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. A long passage that reads as coherent prose: arguments for refusing munitions and money, and renewing the hope of a match with Princess Margarita. The English is faithful. It has more damage than the 1630 letters before it: about eight places restored from stains or tears (Ita[lia], d[i a]ver, giustissi[ma ge]losia, qua[tt]rocento, no[str]a, ne[go]zio), "call" changed to [d]all, and "coni" left doubtful where the sense needs così. Whose son is meant depends on a doubtful clear word.

texts.summary: The marchese's offers may bring requests for money and munitions. The agent gets the arguments for refusing and is to renew the hope of a match with Princess Margarita, the duke's sister.

texts.label: cc. 20r-20v, 1 Mar 1630

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. The cipher is only about 50 words in four short pieces inside clear text. Once normalised, each piece reads coherently with the clear text around it. As decrypted, though, it is raw: "quclificati", "circontanze", "qrincipe" and "crepcnti dc nostri cicscuno" all needed editor changes, and "del principe del principe" is a repetition kept from the writer. That is about seven departures in 50 words, so the readable sense rests on the editor's normalisation.

texts.summary: The agent cannot serve Modena and also handle business for Mirandola and Correggio. The clear text says the Venice courier was robbed at Gradisca and that duplicates are enclosed.
texts.note: Words 50: A 50, B 48, C 42. Read on a one-word margin.

texts.label: c. 23r, 14 Mar 1630

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. Fully coherent Italian with no holes. The decryption matches the reading letter for letter. This letter is the source of the key, and a later clear copy (c. 22) exists, so it is not an independent test of the key.

texts.summary: The agent may inform Carnevale, in general terms only, and must put Modena before the fallen lord of Correggio. Transcription job: c. 22 covers it, and it is the source of the key.
texts.note: Words 68: A, B and C all 68.

texts.label: cc. 73r-74r, 2 Feb 1636

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. The cipher part (resolve to show the front, hold the strongholds, troops sent to Milan) and the two postscripts (His Majesty and Italy; 200,000 scudi at Bologna, Barberini expected) read as coherent Italian, but only after many editor changes. The raw decryption has "nof", "campcgnc", "io questa", "neceuita", "noutro" and "snfriuano", and about a dozen signs under blots were restored. The main cipher sentence ends in a hole: "[?prometterci]" leaves "they suffered in ..." unresolved, and the "sì per" construction there is never completed. Much of the surrounding clear text has doubtful place names and phrases.

texts.summary: French and Savoyard troops enter Modenese land while their envoys are still in the city. The duke will show his front and hold the main strongholds. Postscripts: His Majesty must attend to Italy; 200,000 scudi have reached the legate at Bologna, and Cardinal Antonio Barberini is expected there.
texts.note: Words 154: A 153, B 147, C 136. Read, provisional: no margin on B, and C is 88.3%.

validation.notes: The key was tested in the target's own held-out test (c. 13r, 289 sign positions, against the clear copy c. 15r: 286/289 visual, 232/289 machine with no language; 100-200 shuffled tables at best 43.6%). The n-gram validator was not run.
